[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | Al-Alusi rejects an excuse based on God's foreknowledge or decree: God wrote only what He knew, and knowledge follows what is known, including their poor disposition and resulting choices.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · شبل | reports | Shibl reads شقوتنا with fatḥa on the initial shīn.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وحمزة والكسائي والمفضل عن عاصم وأبان والزعفراني وابن مقسم | reports | These readers have شقاوتنا with fatḥa on shīn and an alif after qāf.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قتادة والحسن عن خالد بن حوشب | reports | Qatada, and al-Hasan in Khalid ibn Hawshab's transmission, read شقاوتنا with alif and kasra on shīn.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | All forms are verbal nouns meaning the opposite of felicity; a group glosses them as the evil end God knew their deeds deserved, a view attributed to most Mu'tazilites.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الأشاعرة | reports | The Ashʿarites interpret their wretchedness as the disbelief and sins God had written for them in eternity.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubba'i understands wretchedness metaphorically as desire and pursuit of pleasures, naming the cause by its effect.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | Rather than personification as a settled agent, the wording is best treated as a representational metaphor: an affair originating in themselves prevailed over them.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | On every account of wretchedness, their words confess that God's proof stood against them: its source was their own condition, so they cannot claim injustice in punishment.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · حمزة والكسائي وخلف | reports | Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read شقاوتنا with fatḥa on the shīn and an alif after the qāf.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r11] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Adding قوما depicts misguidance as a defining trait and part of their collective identity, as in other Qur’anic descriptions of peoples. | mentions 2:164, 10:101
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | غلب is literally to overpower; here it means being overtaken by misery rather than happiness, with the object ‘happiness’ understood from the context.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The object of غلبت is omitted but supplied by شقوتنا: their misery overcame happiness; the following على phrase names what was overcome.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The preposition على after a form of ‘overcome’ marks what is overcome, as in the hadith phrase ‘the men have prevailed over us.’
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Their freely choosing causes of misery over causes of happiness is pictured as a state of inner contest in which misery gained the upper hand; it became theirs as it dominated them.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read شقوتنا with kasra on the shīn and a still qāf.
[TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Wretchedness is the opposite of happiness; a person's allotted good is lost in wretchedness, or wretchedness is the evil that characterizes them.
[TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Their wording that misery overcame them hints that they acquired it through bad choices; their promise to act well if returned confirms that their state relates to voluntary action.
[TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | They imagine themselves as neutral beings overcome by misery, but their misery is their own through bad choices and deeds; this is an admission that the proof against them was complete.
[TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Their confession and denial on Judgment Day merely express settled dispositions: some lie and deny the truth despite seeing it. | mentions 58:18, 40:73-74
[TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · أبو عبد الله | reports | Al-Sadiq explains that their own deeds made them wretched.
[ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | In this context shiqwah means abstract bad luck, the sinners’ futile excuse for their own failings.
[ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | The allegorical dialogue exposes a common excuse and indirectly stresses free will and responsibility for human actions and behavior.
[ASAD-NOTES:23:106/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | The condemned blame their misfortune for leading them astray and beg to leave their suffering, promising to be counted among evildoers if they sin again.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The passage first gives God's response to the damned, then their confession and plea for release.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | At the afterlife judgment, God reminds the disbelievers that they denied His recited revelations; this sin is singled out because their other evils began with that rejection.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Their reply truthfully admits that their evil inclinations dominated them and that they became a misguided people.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Their denial and rebellion arose from failing to overcome appetites, self-interest, and human weakness, not from sincere inquiry or reasoned conclusions.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Their plea to be brought out will go unanswered because they should have made it during worldly life.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | In worldly life, sincere Muslims prayed and prepared for salvation while disbelievers mocked them; now the believers have attained the happy outcome.
[QIRAAT-ER:23:106:5#1/r1] QIRAAT-ER · Lvw | reports | The alternative masdar shaqāwa is a common faʿāla pattern, while shiqwa is the rarer fiʿla; both derive from sh-q-w.
[STUDYQURAN:23:105/r1] STUDYQURAN · R and Z | reports | The verb rendered “overwhelmed” can mean taking possession, ownership, or dominion over something.
[STUDYQURAN:23:105/r2] STUDYQURAN · Ṭ | reports | The disbelievers’ statement is read as describing God’s role in making them wretched, because He decreed their wretchedness in the Mother of the Book. | mentions 43:4
[STUDYQURAN:23:105/r3] STUDYQURAN · Q | reports | On this interpretation, their words are treated as a statement of fact, not a plea.
[STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran. | mentions 7:59, 7:60, 7:61, 7:62, 7:136
[STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
